``` # Set up R & RStudio {.hero #s00c-installation} ::: {.section-badge} Setup · Install the tools ::: ## Install R R is distributed by [CRAN](https://cloud.r-project.org/) — the Comprehensive R Archive Network. :::: {.columns .install-r-columns} ::: {.column width="62%"} ::: {.step-list .step-list-spaced} 1. Run the installer with the OS defaults ::: ::: ::: {.column width="38%"} ```{=html} ``` ::: :::: ::: {.dh-note} Any current **R 4.x** works — new versions ship in **April** and **October** each year. ::: ## Install RStudio RStudio is the IDE (Integrated Development Environment) for R. :::: {.columns .install-rstudio-columns} ::: {.column width="62%"} ::: {.step-list .step-list-spaced} 1. Go to [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) 2. Pick the free **RStudio Desktop** edition 3. Install with your OS defaults 4. RStudio auto-detects your R install ::: ::: ::: {.column width="38%"} ```{=html} ``` ::: :::: ::: {.dh-note} New versions ship every few months. RStudio prompts you on launch when one is available. ::: ## Alternative: Posit Cloud Prefer nothing-to-install? [posit.cloud](https://posit.cloud/) runs RStudio in your browser. :::: {.columns .install-posit-columns} ::: {.column width="62%"} ::: {.step-list .step-list-spaced} 1. Go to [posit.cloud](https://posit.cloud/) 2. Sign in with any email (Google / GitHub / plain) 3. Pick the **free** tier 4. **15 projects**, **1 GB RAM**, and **1 CPU core** ::: ::: ::: {.column width="38%"} ```{=html} ``` ::: :::: ::: {.dh-note} Runs on Linux under the hood — same OS-level surface as RStudio Desktop. ::: # Install packages {.hero #s00d-packages} ::: {.section-badge} Setup · Manage dependencies ::: ## `install.packages()` Install any CRAN package by name: ```r install.packages("tidyquant") ``` This is a **one-time** operation per package per machine, write it directly in the Console, not in a script. Three importers you'll want early: - **`haven`**: Stata `.dta`, SAS `.sas7bdat`, SPSS `.sav` - **`readxl`**: Excel `.xls` / `.xlsx` - **`readr`**: plain-text `.csv`, `.tsv`, fixed-width ## Keeping packages current Check what has updates available: ```r old.packages() ``` Update everything at once: ```r update.packages() ``` Force-reinstall a single package (safer when only one is stuck). * From RStudio: **Tools → Install Packages** for a GUI equivalent. # Scripts & R projects {.hero #s00e-scripts-projects} ::: {.section-badge} Setup · Reproducible workspace ::: ## Why RStudio Projects The working directory is where R looks for files. Check it with: ```r getwd() #> [1] "C:/Users/gabbo/Downloads/deploy-60e3c5ad..." ``` The obvious fix is `setwd()`: ```r setwd("/path/to/my/analysis") ``` **But** that path is machine-specific, **RStudio Projects** solve this: the project's `.Rproj` file marks the folder as the working directory. - **File → New Project → New Directory → New Project**. ## R scripts + `library()` :::: {.type-cards} ::: {.type-card .type-vector} [The script]{.type-card-tag} ### Why a `.R` file? The Console runs one line, then forgets it. An R script is a plain-text file that is - **Reproducible** - **Version-controllable** - **Re-runnable** ::: {.script-hint} Create it: File → New File → R Script  ·  [⌘⇧N]{.kbd} ::: ::: ::: {.type-card .type-list} [The header]{.type-card-tag} ### Load what you need Put every `library()` call at the top: ```r # ---- setup ---- library(readr) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) # ---- analysis ---- read_csv("data/AAPL.csv") # Look up any function's docs ?read_csv ``` ::: :::: # R data structures {.hero #s00f-data-structures} ::: {.section-badge} Basics · Vectors → matrices → data frames ::: ## Dimensionality & homogeneity Base R containers split along two axes, **dimensionality** and whether contents share **one type** or **many**. ::: {.dh-intro} ::: ```{=html}
Homogeneous
Heterogeneous
1d
Atomic vector
List
2d
Matrix
Data frame
nd
Array
—
``` ::: {.dh-note} There is **no scalar type** in R. A single number or string is really a length-1 vector. ::: ## Vectors & lists :::: {.type-cards} ::: {.type-card .type-vector} [Homogeneous · atomic]{.type-card-tag} ### Atomic vector Four flavours: `double`, `integer`, `logical`, `character`. Build one with `c()`. ```{webr-r} dbl_var <- c(1, 2.5, 4.5) int_var <- c(1L, 6L, 10L) log_var <- c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE) chr_var <- c("here is", "a string") ``` ::: ::: {.type-card .type-list} [Heterogeneous · list]{.type-card-tag} ### List Vectors of different types and lengths, other lists, functions. ```{webr-r} list(dbl = c(1, 2.5, 4.5), int = c(1L, 6L, 10L), log = c(TRUE, FALSE), chr = c("here is", "a string")) ``` ::: :::: ## Matrices & arrays {.mx-slide #matrices-arrays} ::: {.mx-stage-wrap}
::: []{.fragment .fi-frag id="mx-frag-tensor"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="mx-frag-s1"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="mx-frag-s2"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="mx-frag-s3"} :::: {.type-cards} ::: {.type-card .type-vector} [2d · matrix]{.type-card-tag} ```{webr-r} a <- matrix(1:4, nrow = 2, ncol = 2) a ``` ::: ::: {.type-card .type-list} [3d · array (tensor)]{.type-card-tag} ```{webr-r} b <- array(1:27, dim = c(3, 3, 3)) dim(b) ``` ::: :::: ## Equivalent verbs, different containers ::: {.verb-intro} Same operation, different function name per container: ::: ::: {.verb-table} | Operation | Vector | Matrix | Array | |:------------------|:--------------------|:-----------------------------|:--------------| | **Naming** | `names()` | `rownames()`, `colnames()` | `dimnames()` | | **Sizing** | `length()` | `nrow()`, `ncol()` | `dim()` | | **Transpose** | — | `t()` | `aperm()` | | **Type test** | `is.null(dim(x))` | `is.matrix()` | `is.array()` | ::: :::: {.type-cards} ::: {.type-card .type-vector} [Try it · name rows]{.type-card-tag} ```{webr-r} rownames(a) <- c("row 1", "row 2") a ``` ::: ::: {.type-card .type-list} […and name cols]{.type-card-tag} ```{webr-r} colnames(a) <- c("col 1", "col 2") a ``` ::: :::: ## Data frames :::: {.type-cards} ::: {.type-card .type-vector} [The idea]{.type-card-tag} ### List of equal-length vectors Columnar heterogeneity of a **list**, rectangular shape of a **matrix** — the shape almost every real dataset in R takes. `ncol()` and `length()` return the same thing: the number of columns. ::: ::: {.type-card .type-list} [In code]{.type-card-tag} ### Build one Pass each column as a named vector argument. ```{webr-r} df1 <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = c("a", "b", "c"), z = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)) df1 ``` Peek at column types with `str(df1)`. ::: :::: ## Tibbles :::: {.type-cards} ::: {.type-card .type-vector} [Better defaults]{.type-card-tag} ### `tibble()` for modern R Same shape as `data.frame`, sharper printing, no silent type coercion. ```{webr-r} #| message: false library(tibble) tibble(x = 1:3, y = c("a", "b", "c"), z = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)) ``` ::: ::: {.type-card .type-list} [Non-syntactic names]{.type-card-tag} ### Backticks let you use any name ```{webr-r} tibble(`:)` = "smile", ` ` = "space", `2000` = "number") ``` `data.frame()` would either mangle these or refuse them. ::: :::: # Subsetting {.hero #s00g-subsetting} ::: {.section-badge} Basics · `[`, `[[`, and `$` ::: ## On data frames and tibbles ```{webr-r} df1 <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = c("a", "b", "c"), z = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)) # a whole column (still a data frame) df1[1] # rows × columns df1[1, 1:2] # a column as a vector (unwrapped) df1$x # the 3rd element of that vector df1$x[3] ``` `df[i]` keeps the data-frame wrapper; `df$x` gives you the raw vector. ## On lists ```{webr-r} list_a <- list(x = 1:3, y = c("a", "b", "c")) # 1st element — still a list of length 1 list_a[1] # 1st element unwrapped — the vector inside list_a[[1]] # then index into that vector list_a[[1]][1] ``` **Rule of thumb:** single brackets `[ ]` preserve the container type; double brackets `[[ ]]` and `$` extract the contents. # Getting financial data {.hero #s01-get-data} ::: {.section-badge} Module 1 · Import (R4DS ch 7) ::: ## The classic way: `tidyquant::tq_get()` Live, from Yahoo Finance: ```r library(tidyquant) aapl <- tq_get("AAPL", from = "2015-01-01", to = "2024-12-31", get = "stock.prices") head(aapl) ``` Fine for exploratory use, but renders need the network. For a reproducible course, we cache to disk once and read from CSV. ## The reproducible way: committed CSVs ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(readr) library(dplyr) aapl <- read_csv("data/AAPL.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) head(aapl, 4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 × 7 date open high low close volume adjusted 1 2015-01-02 27.8 27.9 26.8 27.3 212818400 24.2 2 2015-01-05 27.1 27.2 26.4 26.6 257142000 23.5 3 2015-01-06 26.6 26.9 26.2 26.6 263188400 23.5 4 2015-01-07 26.8 27.0 26.7 26.9 160423600 23.8 ``` ::: ::: Every subsequent module reads from `data/` — no network calls at render time. ## The five tickers you'll see - **AAPL** — Apple, large-cap equity - **MSFT** — Microsoft, another large-cap equity (for correlation stories) - **SPY** — S&P 500 ETF, the market proxy for CAPM - **TLT** — 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF, bond proxy - **GLD** — SPDR Gold Shares, commodity proxy ## Fama-French factors, too ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ff <- read_csv("data/ff_factors.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) head(ff, 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 5 date mkt_rf smb hml rf 1 2015-01-02 -0.0012 -0.0059 0.0012 0 2 2015-01-05 -0.0184 0.0033 -0.0067 0 3 2015-01-06 -0.0103 -0.0079 -0.0029 0 ``` ::: ::: `Mkt-RF`, `SMB`, `HML`, `RF` in decimals (not percent). Used in module 9 for CAPM. # Visualize with ggplot2 {.hero #s02-first-plot} ::: {.section-badge} Module 2 · Visualize (R4DS ch 2) ::: # Candlesticks + moving average {.fp1-slide #demo-first-plot-1} ::: {.section-badge} tidyquant · AAPL monthly candles + SMA(6) ::: ::: {.fi-stage-wrap}
::: []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp1-frag-geom"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp1-frag-overlay"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp1-frag-labs"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp1-frag-theme"} ```{=html} ``` # OHLC bars + moving average {.fp2-slide #demo-first-plot-2} ::: {.section-badge} tidyquant · AAPL monthly bars + SMA(12) ::: ::: {.fi-stage-wrap}
::: []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp2-frag-geom"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp2-frag-overlay"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp2-frag-labs"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp2-frag-theme"} ```{=html} ``` # Line + Bollinger bands {.fp3-slide #demo-first-plot-3} ::: {.section-badge} tidyquant · SPY close + 12-mo bbands (±2σ) ::: ::: {.fi-stage-wrap}
::: []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp3-frag-geom"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp3-frag-overlay"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp3-frag-labs"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp3-frag-theme"} ```{=html} ``` # Four tickers, one facet {.fp4-slide #demo-first-plot-4} ::: {.section-badge} tidyquant · candlesticks · free_y facet ::: ::: {.fi-stage-wrap}
::: []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp4-frag-geom"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp4-frag-labs"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fp4-frag-theme"} ```{=html} ``` # 3 · Transform with dplyr {.hero #s03-transform} ::: {.section-badge} Module 3 · Transform (R4DS ch 4) ::: ## Log returns with `mutate` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(readr); library(dplyr) aapl <- read_csv("data/AAPL.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(log_return = log(adjusted / lag(adjusted))) aapl |> select(date, adjusted, log_return) |> head(4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 × 3 date adjusted log_return 1 2015-01-02 24.2 NA 2 2015-01-05 23.5 -0.0286 3 2015-01-06 23.5 0.0000943 4 2015-01-07 23.8 0.0139 ``` ::: ::: `lag()` shifts the column down by one row so `log(x / lag(x))` yields the daily log return. # dplyr::mutate() {.mu-slide #demo-mutate-slide} ::: {.section-badge} Add a computed column · log returns ::: ::: {.fi-stage-wrap}
::: []{.fragment .fi-frag id="mu-frag-1"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="mu-frag-2"} ```{=html} ``` ## Slice with `filter` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} recent_aapl <- aapl |> filter(date >= as.Date("2024-01-01"), date <= as.Date("2024-03-31")) nrow(recent_aapl) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 61 ``` ::: ::: Combine conditions with `&` (`,` inside `filter` is the same as `&`). # dplyr::filter() {.fi-slide #demo-filter-slide} ::: {.section-badge} Two conditions · ticker and date ::: ::: {.fi-stage-wrap}
::: []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fi-cond-1"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fi-cond-2"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fi-both"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="fi-arrows"} ```{=html} ``` ## Per-ticker summaries with `group_by` + `summarise` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(purrr) prices <- map_dfr(c("AAPL", "MSFT", "SPY", "TLT", "GLD"), ~ read_csv(paste0("data/", .x, ".csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(ticker = .x, log_return = log(adjusted / lag(adjusted)))) prices |> group_by(ticker) |> summarise( n = n(), mean_ret = mean(log_return, na.rm = TRUE), sd_ret = sd(log_return, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 5 × 4 ticker n mean_ret sd_ret 1 AAPL 2515 0.000930 0.0179 2 GLD 2515 0.000297 0.00890 3 MSFT 2515 0.000938 0.0171 4 SPY 2515 0.000488 0.0111 5 TLT 2515 -0.0000477 0.00965 ``` ::: ::: Five rows out — one per ticker. # 4 · Tidy with tidyr {.hero #s04-tidy} ::: {.section-badge} Module 4 · Tidy (R4DS ch 5) ::: ## Wide → long with `pivot_longer` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(readr); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(purrr) # Start wide: one column per ticker's adjusted close wide <- map(c("AAPL", "MSFT", "SPY"), ~ read_csv(paste0("data/", .x, ".csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |> select(date, all_of("adjusted")) |> rename(!!.x := adjusted)) |> reduce(inner_join, by = "date") head(wide, 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 4 date AAPL MSFT SPY 1 2015-01-02 24.2 39.7 170. 2 2015-01-05 23.5 39.3 167. 3 2015-01-06 23.5 38.7 165. ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Pivot to long — one row per (date, ticker) long <- wide |> pivot_longer(cols = -date, names_to = "ticker", values_to = "close") head(long, 6) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 3 date ticker close 1 2015-01-02 AAPL 24.2 2 2015-01-02 MSFT 39.7 3 2015-01-02 SPY 170. 4 2015-01-05 AAPL 23.5 5 2015-01-05 MSFT 39.3 6 2015-01-05 SPY 167. ``` ::: ::: Long form is what `group_by(ticker)` wants. # tidyr::pivot_longer() {.pl-slide #demo-pivot-longer-slide} ::: {.section-badge} Wide → long · one column per ticker becomes rows ::: ::: {.fi-stage-wrap}
::: []{.fragment .fi-frag id="pl-frag-1"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="pl-frag-2"} ```{=html} ``` ## Long → wide with `pivot_wider` Sometimes you want the other direction — e.g. to compute a correlation matrix. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} returns_long <- long |> group_by(ticker) |> arrange(date) |> mutate(log_return = log(close / lag(close))) |> ungroup() |> filter(!is.na(log_return)) returns_wide <- returns_long |> select(date, ticker, log_return) |> pivot_wider(names_from = ticker, values_from = log_return) head(returns_wide, 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 4 date AAPL MSFT SPY 1 2015-01-05 -0.0286 -0.00924 -0.0182 2 2015-01-06 0.0000943 -0.0148 -0.00946 3 2015-01-07 0.0139 0.0126 0.0124 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Correlation matrix over the wide format cor(returns_wide |> select(-date), use = "complete.obs") |> round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` AAPL MSFT SPY AAPL 1.000 0.685 0.749 MSFT 0.685 1.000 0.797 SPY 0.749 0.797 1.000 ``` ::: ::: Wide when you want cross-column math (correlations, portfolio returns from weight × ticker matrices). # tidyr::pivot_wider() {.pw-slide #demo-pivot-wider-slide} ::: {.section-badge} Long → wide · one row per date, one column per ticker ::: ::: {.fi-stage-wrap}
::: []{.fragment .fi-frag id="pw-frag-1"} []{.fragment .fi-frag id="pw-frag-2"} ```{=html} ``` # 5 · Pipes & workflow {.hero #s05-workflow} ::: {.section-badge} Module 5 · Workflow (R4DS ch 3, 6) ::: ## Same pipeline, three ways Nested (unreadable): ```r head( filter( mutate( read_csv("data/AAPL.csv"), log_return = log(adjusted / lag(adjusted))), date >= "2024-01-01"), 5) ``` Assignment-heavy (verbose): ```r aapl <- read_csv("data/AAPL.csv") aapl <- mutate(aapl, log_return = log(adjusted / lag(adjusted))) aapl <- filter(aapl, date >= "2024-01-01") head(aapl, 5) ``` Piped (read top-to-bottom like a recipe): ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(readr); library(dplyr) read_csv("data/AAPL.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(log_return = log(adjusted / lag(adjusted))) |> filter(date >= as.Date("2024-01-01")) |> head(5) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 5 × 8 date open high low close volume adjusted log_return 1 2024-01-02 187. 188. 184. 186. 82488700 184. -0.0364 2 2024-01-03 184. 186. 183. 184. 58414500 182. -0.00752 3 2024-01-04 182. 183. 181. 182. 71983600 180. -0.0128 4 2024-01-05 182. 183. 180. 181. 62379700 179. -0.00402 5 2024-01-08 182. 186. 182. 186. 59144500 183. 0.0239 ``` ::: ::: ## Style checklist - **One verb per line** — the pipe should read as a sequence of steps - **Indent continuation lines** — 2 spaces after `|>` - **Meaningful names** — `daily_returns`, not `df2` - **Snake_case for objects and columns** — `log_return`, not `LogReturn` - **Use projects, not `setwd()`** — the working directory is the `.Rproj` folder # 6 · Dates & time series {.hero #s06-dates-ts} ::: {.section-badge} Module 6 · Dates in R ::: ## Parsing and formatting ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(lubridate) d <- ymd("2024-06-30") class(d) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Date" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} year(d); month(d); day(d); wday(d, label = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 2024 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 6 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 30 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] Sun Levels: Sun < Mon < Tue < Wed < Thu < Fri < Sat ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} d + months(3) # forward three months ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "2024-09-30" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} d - years(1) # a year ago ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "2023-06-30" ``` ::: ::: ## Rolling averages with `zoo::rollmean` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(readr); library(dplyr); library(zoo) aapl <- read_csv("data/AAPL.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate( ma_20 = rollmean(adjusted, k = 20, fill = NA, align = "right"), ma_60 = rollmean(adjusted, k = 60, fill = NA, align = "right"), ma_200 = rollmean(adjusted, k = 200, fill = NA, align = "right") ) aapl |> select(date, adjusted, ma_20, ma_60, ma_200) |> tail(4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 × 5 date adjusted ma_20 ma_60 ma_200 1 2024-12-24 257. 245. 233. 210. 2 2024-12-26 257. 246. 233. 211. 3 2024-12-27 254. 247. 234. 211. 4 2024-12-30 251. 248. 234. 211. ``` ::: ::: `align = "right"` means the moving average at date *t* uses the *k* prior days including *t* — the causal convention traders use. ## Quick moving-average chart ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ggplot2); library(tidyr) aapl |> select(date, adjusted, ma_60, ma_200) |> pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |> ggplot(aes(date, value, colour = series)) + geom_line() + theme_minimal() + labs(title = "AAPL price with 60-day and 200-day moving averages", x = NULL, y = "USD", colour = NULL) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-11-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: # 7 · Write your own functions {.hero #s07-functions} ::: {.section-badge} Module 7 · Program (R4DS ch 25) ::: ## Anatomy ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} sharpe_ratio <- function(returns, rf = 0, freq = 252) { excess <- returns - rf / freq mean(excess, na.rm = TRUE) / sd(excess, na.rm = TRUE) * sqrt(freq) } # Try it on AAPL daily log returns library(readr); library(dplyr) aapl_ret <- read_csv("data/AAPL.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(r = log(adjusted / lag(adjusted))) |> pull(r) sharpe_ratio(aapl_ret) |> round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.823 ``` ::: ::: ## Maximum drawdown ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} max_drawdown <- function(returns) { cum <- cumprod(1 + returns[!is.na(returns)]) peaks <- cummax(cum) min((cum - peaks) / peaks) } max_drawdown(aapl_ret) |> round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] -0.402 ``` ::: ::: Interpretation: the largest peak-to-trough loss you'd have experienced holding AAPL over the full sample. ## Compare to a library implementation ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(PerformanceAnalytics) # PerformanceAnalytics expects an xts; convert quickly aapl_xts <- read_csv("data/AAPL.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(r = log(adjusted / lag(adjusted))) |> filter(!is.na(r)) |> { \(d) xts::xts(d$r, order.by = d$date) }() SharpeRatio.annualized(aapl_xts, Rf = 0) |> round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] Annualized Sharpe Ratio (Rf=0%, p=95%): 0.823 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} maxDrawdown(aapl_xts) |> round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.402 ``` ::: ::: The numbers should match your homemade functions to within rounding. # 8 · Iterate across tickers {.hero #s08-iteration} ::: {.section-badge} Module 8 · Iteration (R4DS ch 26) ::: ## Compute Sharpe for every ticker in one line ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(readr); library(dplyr); library(purrr) sharpe_ratio <- function(returns, rf = 0, freq = 252) { excess <- returns - rf / freq mean(excess, na.rm = TRUE) / sd(excess, na.rm = TRUE) * sqrt(freq) } tickers <- c("AAPL", "MSFT", "SPY", "TLT", "GLD") summary_tbl <- map_dfr(tickers, function (tk) { path <- paste0("data/", tk, ".csv") r <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(r = log(adjusted / lag(adjusted))) |> pull(r) tibble( ticker = tk, n = sum(!is.na(r)), mean = mean(r, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(r, na.rm = TRUE), sharpe = sharpe_ratio(r) ) }) summary_tbl |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, 4)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 5 × 5 ticker n mean sd sharpe 1 AAPL 2514 0.0009 0.0179 0.823 2 MSFT 2514 0.0009 0.0171 0.871 3 SPY 2514 0.0005 0.0111 0.695 4 TLT 2514 0 0.0096 -0.0784 5 GLD 2514 0.0003 0.0089 0.530 ``` ::: ::: Five rows out, one per ticker. Change the ticker vector — nothing else changes. ## Why `map_dfr` and not `for` - `map_dfr` gives you a tibble automatically — no manual `rbind` or pre-allocation - Errors point at the item that failed (`try(map_dfr, ...)`) — easy to catch a single bad ticker - It composes: `map_dfr(x, f) |> filter(...)` reads cleanly # 9 · Linear regression: CAPM {.hero #s09-capm} ::: {.section-badge} Module 9 · Model (R4DS light) ::: ## Load the pieces ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(readr); library(dplyr); library(broom); library(lubridate) # AAPL excess returns aapl <- read_csv("data/AAPL.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(r_aapl = log(adjusted / lag(adjusted))) |> select(date, r_aapl) ff <- read_csv("data/ff_factors.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> select(date, mkt_rf, rf) capm_data <- inner_join(aapl, ff, by = "date") |> mutate(r_aapl_excess = r_aapl - rf) |> filter(!is.na(r_aapl_excess)) head(capm_data, 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 5 date r_aapl mkt_rf rf r_aapl_excess 1 2015-01-05 -0.0286 -0.0184 0 -0.0286 2 2015-01-06 0.0000943 -0.0103 0 0.0000943 3 2015-01-07 0.0139 0.0119 0 0.0139 ``` ::: ::: ## Fit the regression ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} fit <- lm(r_aapl_excess ~ mkt_rf, data = capm_data) summary(fit) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: lm(formula = r_aapl_excess ~ mkt_rf, data = capm_data) Residuals: Min 1Q Median 3Q Max -0.076974 -0.006242 -0.000182 0.005930 0.092088 Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) 0.0003014 0.0002399 1.256 0.209 mkt_rf 1.1572280 0.0208350 55.542 <2e-16 *** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 Residual standard error: 0.01202 on 2512 degrees of freedom Multiple R-squared: 0.5512, Adjusted R-squared: 0.551 F-statistic: 3085 on 1 and 2512 DF, p-value: < 2.2e-16 ``` ::: ::: ## Read the coefficients ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} tidy(fit) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 5 term estimate std.error statistic p.value 1 (Intercept) 0.000301 0.000240 1.26 0.209 2 mkt_rf 1.16 0.0208 55.5 0 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} glance(fit) |> select(r.squared, adj.r.squared, sigma, statistic, p.value) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 5 r.squared adj.r.squared sigma statistic p.value 1 0.551 0.551 0.0120 3085. 0 ``` ::: ::: - **Intercept** (`alpha`) — the "excess" return AAPL earns per day beyond what CAPM predicts. Statistically indistinguishable from zero here. - **Slope** (`beta`) — how much AAPL moves for each 1% move in the excess market return. β ≈ 1.2 means AAPL is somewhat more volatile than the market. - **R²** — fraction of AAPL's daily variance explained by the market. ~0.4 for a large-cap tech name is typical. ## Extend to a factor model (three factors) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ff_full <- read_csv("data/ff_factors.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) capm3 <- inner_join(aapl, ff_full, by = "date") |> mutate(r_aapl_excess = r_aapl - rf) |> filter(!is.na(r_aapl_excess)) lm(r_aapl_excess ~ mkt_rf + smb + hml, data = capm3) |> tidy() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 × 5 term estimate std.error statistic p.value 1 (Intercept) 0.000237 0.000226 1.05 2.94e- 1 2 mkt_rf 1.17 0.0201 58.4 0 3 smb -0.297 0.0352 -8.45 4.93e-17 4 hml -0.400 0.0250 -16.0 7.93e-55 ``` ::: ::: Same one-line change adds `SMB` (size) and `HML` (value) — the Fama-French 3-factor model. # 10 · Communicate with Quarto {.hero #s10-communicate} ::: {.section-badge} Module 10 · Communicate (R4DS ch 29) ::: ## The minimum Create `report.qmd`: ````r --- title: "AAPL: a mini portfolio note" author: "Gabriel Cabrera" format: html execute: echo: true warning: false --- ## Setup ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(readr); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2) aapl <- read_csv("data/AAPL.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) ``` ::: ## Price history ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(aapl, aes(date, adjusted)) + geom_line() + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-21-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=672} ::: ::: ## Summary - Mean daily log return: 9.3\times 10^{-4} ```` Then in the terminal: ``` quarto render report.qmd ``` ## Publication-grade tables with `gt` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(gt) capm_results <- tibble( ticker = c("AAPL", "MSFT", "SPY", "GLD"), alpha = c(0.0002, 0.0001, 0.0000, 0.0001), beta = c(1.21, 1.09, 1.00, 0.06), r2 = c(0.42, 0.51, 1.00, 0.02) ) capm_results |> gt() |> tab_header(title = "CAPM regression summary") |> fmt_number(columns = c(alpha), decimals = 4) |> fmt_number(columns = c(beta, r2), decimals = 2) |> cols_label(ticker = "Ticker", alpha = "α", beta = "β", r2 = "R²") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
CAPM regression summary
Ticker α β R²
AAPL 0.0002 1.21 0.42

SPY 0.0000 1.00 1.00
GLD 0.0001 0.06 0.02
``` ::: ::: ## Ship the whole analysis Pick your output format in the YAML: ```yaml format: revealjs # for a slide deck like this one format: html # for a notebook-style report format: pdf # for a printable PDF format: docx # for a Word document ``` Same `.qmd`, four different outputs. Add `execute: freeze: auto` to cache chunk results so successive renders only re-run edited chunks. # Resources {.hero #s11-resources} ::: {.section-badge} Module 11 · Where to go next ::: ## Books to read next - **R for Data Science, 2e** — Wickham, Çetinkaya-Rundel & Grolemund [r4ds.hadley.nz](https://r4ds.hadley.nz) — the source structure of this course - **Reproducible Finance with R** — Regenstein [github.com/reproducible-finance](https://github.com/reproducible-finance) — R workflows for portfolio math - **Advanced R** — Wickham [adv-r.hadley.nz](https://adv-r.hadley.nz) — for when you want to understand the language, not just use it - **Applied Quantitative Finance** — Härdle, Franke, Hafner Formal treatment of the finance math behind CAPM, factor models, GARCH ## Packages worth learning after this course - `tidyquant` — everything financial in a tidyverse-native API - `PerformanceAnalytics` — Sharpe / Sortino / drawdown / CAPM one-liners - `xts`, `zoo` — the classical time-series containers - `tsibble`, `fable` — modern tidy time-series forecasting - `quantmod` — market data + technical indicators - `PortfolioAnalytics` — mean-variance and beyond - `rugarch` — GARCH family for volatility modelling ## References for the data - Yahoo Finance — daily OHLCV via `tidyquant::tq_get()` - Kenneth French's data library — Fama-French factors, momentum, industry portfolios via `tidyquant::tq_get(get = "famafrench")` - FRED — macro series (rates, CPI) via `tidyquant::tq_get(get = "economic.data")`

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
